title: Why do indie directors commonly land jobs directing large franchise films?

commenti.body: [removed]

This is not my own theory but it has the ring of truth to it. Marvel movies are a producer's medium not a directors. The only genuine auter in the MCU is Kevin Feige. So they hire directors without enough clout to rock the boat. 

I'd also suggest they're not really interesting movies to make from a directorial stand point. Too many creative decisions have been baked in.
I've always wondered this as well. Look at The Marvels: Why do producers feel comfortable handing off an MCU film with a 300m plus budget to someone who's only directed stuff that's 10x smaller?

As the other commenter said, it’s because the Marvel movies are more like branded content than artistic expression pieces. They bring in names with clout, and then don’t let them actually do anything. I believe the director of the Eternals talked about how she was only there to direct the actors in dialogue scenes and everything else was handled by other people.
[removed]
There is no genuine auteur when it comes to marvel at all.
That's fair, it's pure corporate product.

They're not handing anything off. DaCosta and others have said that Feige and the producers are the ones with actual creative control. The MCU is made in the same mode of production as most TV shows where the showrunner (Feige and co.) is the one with actual control and directors are mostly there to follow orders and handle the day to day work on set.

They hire younger/less experienced directors because they're easier to control and cheaper to hire, it's a pure business decision.
Why the fuck would anyone consider Feige an auteur?!?! What has he directed??

I think you could also ask the question of, who else are they going to hire?

Who actually has experience making a $200+M movie? There really aren't that many directors who have worked in that range. Especially before Marvel started hiring these indie directors. And if a director has already had big budget box office success, they almost definitely have more latitude to get financing and work on their own passion projects rather than working on some preexisting IP that they aren't particularly interested in. There's a reason Chistopher Nolan and Peter Jackson aren't making those kinds of movies - because they already did and don't have to anymore.

Auteur theory doesn’t only apply to directors, it simply means that someone exerts total control over a movie so their vision is communicated to the audience. Nia DaCosta who directed The Marvels said that it was Feige’s movie and that she had to step back and let him have control.
[removed]

Because they are cheap—they generally have less leverage to negotiate salary / final cut, while presumably still getting to make more money than where they were before. Experienced directors just cost more and have more power to exert control.
Nah, he just happens to be an auteur of focus tested corporate schlock.
This is Chloé Zhao erasure.

They’re buying artistic credibility. They can turn around and more easily market their movies as being deep and important because the director they have just made a movie that won awards because of that.

I don't think that holds true for two reasons:

A: if that was the case they would hire journeyman directors with a proven track record in big budget films but without a distinct style (eg Ron Howard, Chris Columbus) rather than indie filmakers noted for having their own style/voice (eg Edgar Wright, Taika Waititi, Sam Raimi, James Gunn)

B: The first MCU film was directed by an indie director (Jon Favreau off the back of Swingers) and was hugely successful, I think they've been sticking to that model ever since because it worked the first time.

Some film critics and theorists expand the idea of auteur beyond just directors to any film maker who has created a consistent body of work with a large degree of control over those works. 

I've seen arguments that Tom Cruise and Arnold Schwartzenegger are auteurs for their specific brands of action films. Or that Adam Sandler is an auteur as both actor and producer for his long and consistent string of comedies. And Kevin Feige could certainly fall into that role for producing such a large volume of films with such a constant style and tone.

>I used to figure that directing would involve "working your way up the ladder" in terms of what you get to make. But I guess not

Mid budget films have largely disappeared though, so the middle step on that ladder doesn't really exist anymore
In the old Hollywood system producers like Selznick or Thalberg were considered to be the major authors of their films, so there's definitely precedent for the idea.

From all the available information that is known about the Marvel films, before directors are even considered for the project, basically the whole thing has mostly be previsualised and the script very near completion. 

The indie directors who sign on to these projects get very little to no say creatively in them. Usually when their style shows up, it’s in the dialogue (eg. James Gunn, Taika Waititi). The Eternals had some shots of grass? Which I guess is Chloe Zhao’s MO. 

Action scenes are almost always handed off to second unit, and in some cases it MASSIVELY shows because it looks like they were shot years apart, by totally different people in some cases like The Marvels. 

The directors seem mostly there to keep the cast happy and to direct performance more than anything else, imo. 

The reason they get smaller directors is because studio directors have a lot more clout and influence to make the film in their vision, which Kevin Feige absolutely does not want. As such, he hires people with little to no pull to faithfully execute something that has already been decided. 

Many of the indie directors hired for the large films seem fine with this as well. They get to hand off creative control for what is no doubt a massive pay check for them, and they get their name out there in the process, and are then get to say they made a film that made hundreds of millions, if not billions of dollars.
[deleted]

Even more... they use the same action team for all the action in all these movies.

It's just not your typical director gig we think of.

In the 90's, these large action films tended to bring in music video/commercial directors that sometimes hadn't even directed an actual film yet.  It's not that dissimilar - it's just the parameters have changed with the "Marvel formula."
Doug Liman directed Swingers. They hired Favreau off the back of Elf.

Oh you're quite right, he wrote Swingers but didn't direct it. I think his work on Zathura was the main reason he was hired for Iron Man.

I was thinking of the fact that Robert Downey Jr has said he signed on to the film because he was a fan of Swingers...
